scenario: AITA for making a Facebook post about someone without telling them? | My (22F) best friend (21M) recently went on a 3 month long trip to India to do volunteer work. He helped to build a water pipeline and taught kids in a local school about hygiene and sanitation. He also paid for the whole trip himself, costing over $3000. He is a pretty shy and quiet guy, so he didn’t tell many people about it before he left and I doubt he was going to when he got back if I didn’t do this. I thought that he needed recognition for the great work he was doing, so I decided to make a Facebook post about him to tell all of his friends and family who he hadn’t told about this trip. I did this while he was away, about a week before he got home. Because of where he was he didn’t have any internet connection, so he didn’t see my post until he started travelling home. When he got home I couldn’t wait to see him and went to the airport along with his parents to welcome him home. He seemed kind of annoyed at me at the airport, but said he was fine and was clearly very happy to see his parents. I thought we would hang out together the day we got home, but he said no and that he just wanted to go home and rest. I decided to text him that evening to ask again what was wrong. He told me he was pissed off at me for the Facebook post. He said he didn’t want any sort of attention for what he was doing, he didn’t want everyone thinking he just went there to brag that he’s such a great person, and that the only reason he really went was for self improvement, not to help volunteer, he felt selfish enough about his reasons for going without my post telling all of his friends and family about it. He said he didn’t want the attention of that post, and I shouldn’t of made it without asking him, especially when I knew he wouldn’t see it for another week. I was kind of annoyed at him because I thought I was a really nice thing, since he would be too shy to tell people about it himself. The post was so positive about him, I didn’t say anything bad. AITA for making that post?

message.reasoning:
Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the action in this scenario is morally acceptable or not. Let me break it down step by step.

First, the situation: The user is a 22-year-old woman whose best friend, a 21-year-old man, went on a three-month trip to India to volunteer. He built a water pipeline, taught kids about hygiene, and paid over $3000 himself. He's shy and quiet, so he didn't tell many people about it before leaving, and the user didn't think he'd tell others upon return. She decided to make a Facebook post about him to give him recognition. She did this while he was away, about a week before he came home. He didn't have internet access there, so he saw the post only when he started traveling home. When he returned, she went to the airport with his parents to welcome him. He seemed annoyed but said he was fine. They didn't hang out that day; he wanted to rest. She texted him that evening, and he told her he was pissed off about the post. He didn't want attention, felt it made him look like he was bragging, and his main reason was self-improvement, not just volunteering. He felt the post was unnecessary and that she shouldn't have done it without asking, especially knowing he wouldn't see it for a week.

The user is asking if she's AITA (Are You the Asshole) for making that post.

So, the key points are:

1. She made a Facebook post about her friend's volunteer trip without his knowledge.
2. He's shy and wouldn't have told others himself.
3. She thought it was a nice thing to do to give him recognition.
4. He was upset because he didn't want attention, felt it misrepresented his reasons, and she didn't ask him first.

Now, evaluating the morality of her action. Morally acceptable or not?

I think the main issue here is consent. She shared something about him without his permission. Even though she had good intentions, respecting his privacy and his wishes is important. He made it clear he didn't want attention, and she went against that by posting about him.

Another point is the potential misrepresentation. She highlighted his volunteer work, but he felt his main reason was self-improvement, not just to help others. By focusing on the volunteer aspect, she might have given others the impression that his primary motive was different from what he felt it was.

Additionally, she knew he wouldn't see the post for a week, so she couldn't get his input before posting. That adds to the issue because she didn't give him a chance to agree or disagree before sharing.

So, considering all these factors, her action might be seen as morally unacceptable because it disregarded his privacy and his expressed wishes. Even though her intentions were good, respecting his boundaries is more important in this context.
